title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness and starvation prevention with adaptive timeouts
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: In production workloads we observed occasional starvation of low-priority queues and increased tail latency under mixed workloads due to fixed scheduling timeouts and coarse queue ordering. This PR tunes the continuous-batcher scheduler to improve queueing fairness and prevent starvation while preserving throughput. It introduces adaptive per-queue timeouts based on recent queue latency percentiles, a lightweight priority aging mechanism to rotate heavily-deferred queues back into service, and small preemption and batching window adjustments to reduce head-of-line blocking. Changes are backwards compatible and guarded behind feature flags for rollout. The goal is to reduce 99th/99.9th percentile latency spikes without regressing average throughput.
commits: feat(scheduler): add adaptive timeout computation from queue latency p50/p95/p99
feat(scheduler): implement priority aging and age-based queue weight adjustments
perf(batcher): reduce batching window for high-contention queues to avoid head-of-line blocking
test(batcher): add unit tests for timeout heuristics and aging behavior
docs: describe new scheduler knobs and rollout guidance in continuous-batcher README
files_changed_summary: services/continuous-batcher/scheduler.go - core scheduling logic updated with timeout heuristics and aging (approx 280 additions/70 deletions)
services/continuous-batcher/config.yaml - new feature flags and fine-grained knobs: adaptive_timeouts, aging_threshold_ms, preemption_fraction
services/continuous-batcher/scheduler_test.go - new unit and table-driven tests for starvation scenarios
perf-canary/jobs/continuous-batcher/ci.yaml - integration scenario added to exercise mixed-priority workloads
docs/continuous-batcher/scheduler.md - operational guidance and recommended rollout steps
metrics/registry.go - new observability counters and histograms for per-queue wait times and age events
review_comments: Marco Rivera (review): Can you explain how the adaptive timeout avoids oscillation when workloads shift rapidly? Also please add an integration test covering a sudden spike in priority traffic.

Aisha Patel (author): The adaptive timeout uses an exponential moving average with a bounded growth factor and a minimum floor; rapid shifts are damped by the EMA tau and we included a short cooldown window before growing timeouts. Added an integration scenario in perf-canary to simulate a sudden priority spike (see perf-canary job).
Lin Chen (review): Nit: prefer configuration knob names with consistent suffixes (e.g., _ms for time values). Also request clearer metric labels for age events.
Aisha Patel (author): Renamed knobs to include units and updated metric names to queue_age_events_total and queue_wait_histogram_ms. Updated docs accordingly.
Priya Desai (approver): Verified local perf runs against the canary scenario. 99th latency reduced ~18% on A100 pools and no throughput regression observed. Approving.
merge_commit_message: squash: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for fairness and starvation prevention\n\nAdaptive timeouts, priority aging, batching window adjustments, tests, and docs
release_notes: Improved continuous-batcher scheduler fairness: adaptive per-queue timeouts to reduce tail latency; priority aging to prevent prolonged starvation of low-priority queues; new config knobs (adaptive_timeouts_enabled, aging_threshold_ms, preemption_fraction) and metrics (queue_wait_histogram_ms, queue_age_events_total). Backwards compatible and rollout gated by feature flag.
notes_for_ops: Rollout plan: enable feature flag in canary for 24h, monitor queue_wait_histogram_ms and request_latency_99p. If tail latency rises or throughput drops >5% within 1h, rollback the feature flag. Recommended knob defaults are included in services/continuous-batcher/config.yaml.
